Primary concern: the validation-to-test coverage gap is 27.5 pp (80.0% → 52.5%). The threshold was set on validation to retain 80% of samples, but on test the model abstains on 47.5%. architecture_research.analysis: The task operates on 28×28×3 images with ~90k training samples and a moderate class imbalance (1.63×). Three architectural facts dominate the design space. (1) Spatial resolution is extremely small: a 7×7 stride-2 first convolution (as in resnet18) immediately collapses 28→14→7, leaving only 49 spatial positions after the first block, which wastes the deeper layers' capacity. (2) Channel statistics are highly asymmetric—means range from 0.53 to 0.74 and stds from 0.12 to 0.18—so per-channel normalisation is not optional; it is the single highest-leverage preprocessing step. The low overall variance (all stds < 0.18) implies that discriminative signal is subtle and concentrated, favouring architectures with strong local feature extraction and careful normalisation over architectures that rely on global context from the outset. (3) The dataset size (~90k) is comfortable for CNNs but tight for full-scale transformers, especially given the imbalance which effectively reduces the minority-class sample count. Architecture ranking: residual_cnn is the strongest default because 2–4 residual blocks with 32→64→128 channels exploit local structure at 28×28 without over-parameterisation, and skip connections stabilise training at this depth. tiny_cnn serves as a fast, low-risk baseline for hyperparameter sweeps. compact_transformer is the preferred transformer entry point: with patch_size=4 it yields 49 tokens, which is enough for meaningful self-attention while keeping the parameter count modest. vision_transformer is viable only if patch_size is reduced to 2 (196 tokens) and depth is capped at 4–6 layers; otherwise the token count is too small for the attention mechanism to learn useful relational structure. resnet18 is the least suitable: its stem is designed for 224×224 inputs and will destroy spatial information at 28×28 unless the first conv is replaced with a 3×3 stride-1 kernel. For the 1.63× imbalance, class-weighted cross-entropy or focal loss (γ=1–2) should be the default, and the validation set (10k) is large enough to monitor per-class recall without overfitting to the metric. The cited evidence (efficient transformer design, small-image representation learning) supports the conclusion that at this resolution, inductive bias from convolutional locality outperforms pure attention unless the transformer is explicitly compacted.
parametrization_priorities: Learning rate: start at 1e-3 for CNNs, 3e-4 for transformers; use cosine or step decay with warmup of 5–10 epochs
Weight decay: 1e-4 to 5e-4 for CNNs; 0.05 for transformer (AdamW decoupled)
Batch size: 128–256 for CNNs; 64–128 for transformers (smaller to stabilise attention gradients with few tokens)
Dropout: 0.2–0.3 on classifier head; stochastic depth 0.1–0.2 in residual blocks; avoid heavy dropout in early conv layers at 28×28
Class-weighted loss or focal loss (γ=1.5) to address the 1.63× imbalance; monitor per-class F1 on validation
For transformers: num_heads=4–8, MLP expansion ratio=2–4, num_layers=4–6 (compact) or 8–12 (full ViT); keep d_model ≤ 192 to match the small token count
For CNNs: channel progression 32→64→128→256 with 2–4 residual blocks; kernel size 3×3 throughout
Early stopping patience of 5–8 epochs on validation loss; track both accuracy and macro-F1
representation_priorities: Per-channel normalisation using the provided means [0.7405, 0.5330, 0.7058] and stds [0.1237, 0.1768, 0.1244] before any model input; do not use global mean/std
Preserve full 28×28 spatial resolution through at least the first two feature-extraction stages; avoid stride-2 downsampling before the second block
For transformer variants, use patch_size=4 (49 tokens) as the default; patch_size=2 (196 tokens) only if attention quality is insufficient
Add a lightweight spatial attention or channel-attention (SE-style) module after the second conv block to compensate for the low channel variance and subtle features
Use global average pooling (not max pooling) before the classifier to retain soft spatial information at 28×28
Consider a 1×1 conv 'bottleneck' before the classifier to mix channels without further spatial reduction
If using residual blocks, keep the number of spatial downsampling steps to at most 2 (28→14→7) to retain enough spatial context
Apply data augmentation (random horizontal flip, small rotation ±10°, mild colour jitter) to counteract the low channel variance and reduce overfitting on the 90k samples
risks: Over-parameterisation: resnet18 or a deep ViT on 28×28 images will have more parameters than useful spatial information, leading to overfitting on 90k samples
Token starvation: transformer attention with <50 tokens may degenerate to near-uniform mixing, providing no advantage over a fully-connected layer
Class imbalance masking: overall accuracy may look acceptable while minority-class recall is poor; always track macro-F1 and per-class confusion

Channel variance suppression: the low stds (0.12–0.18) mean that without per-channel normalisation, the model may latch onto the brighter channel (R, mean 0.74) and ignore the more informative G channel (std 0.18)
Premature spatial collapse: any architecture that downsamples below 7×7 before the final pooling loses the spatial detail that 28×28 images carry
Hyperparameter transfer failure: learning rates and weight decay tuned for 224×224 ImageNet-style training will be poorly calibrated for 28×28; re-sweep is mandatory

Validation set leakage risk: with only 10k validation samples and 1.63× imbalance, a few hundred misclassified minority samples can swing the metric; use stratified splits and report confidence intervals
Transformer training instability at low token counts: attention logits can become poorly conditioned with 49 tokens; use pre-norm, gradient clipping (1.0), and a lower peak LR than CNNs
architecture_research.transformer_guidance: At 28×28 the token budget is the binding constraint. With patch_size=4 the sequence length is 49, which is below the typical 196–576 tokens where self-attention learns rich relational structure. Therefore: (a) prefer compact_transformer over vision_transformer—its reduced d_model (64–128) and fewer layers (4–6) are better matched to 49 tokens and the 90k sample budget. (b) If using vision_transformer, set patch_size=2 to obtain 196 tokens, cap depth at 8 layers, d_model=192, heads=6, and add a learnable position embedding (not sinusoidal, since the grid is only 14×14). (c) Add a convolutional stem (2–3 layers of 3×3 conv with stride 2) before the patch embedding to inject local inductive bias; this hybrid 'conv-stem + transformer' pattern is well-supported by the cited efficient-transformer literature and is critical at this resolution. (d) Use LayerNorm (pre-norm) rather than PostNorm for training stability with few tokens. (e) Attention dropout of 0.1 and MLP dropout of 0.1 are sufficient; avoid heavier regularisation that would suppress the already-limited attention signal. (f) Do NOT use resnet18's 7×7 stride-2 stem as a transformer front-end—it destroys 75% of spatial information before the first attention layer. (g) If compute allows, run a small ablation: patch_size 2 vs 4, with and without conv stem, to confirm the token-count hypothesis before committing to a full search.

representation.rationale: Refinement of the best prior config (res_cnn_base, 0.9875 val_acc). Key changes: (1) hidden 64→80 adds ~25% channel capacity without reaching the 96 that overfit at depth 6; (2) dropout 0.2→0.15 because all top configs converged by epoch 3, indicating the model is not overfitting and lighter regularization allows sharper features; (3) lr 0.001→0.0015 explores the log-scale neighborhood — the SGD/one_cycle variant at lr=0.01 achieved 0.9870, suggesting the adamw optimum may be slightly above 0.001; (4) label_smoothing 0.1→0.05 because the model already achieves 0.9875 balanced accuracy, and excessive smoothing may blunt the decision boundary on the 1.63× imbalanced classes; (5) adding 'contrast' augmentation directly targets the low channel variance (stds 0.12–0.18) by amplifying subtle inter-class differences in the G channel (highest std 0.177). Retains adamw+cosine+batch128+standardize+class_weighting as the proven backbone.

data_profile.ambiguity_note: Several concrete ambiguities and dataset-shift risks are present. (1) Label ambiguity: 'debris' is not a standard histological entity and overlaps heavily with 'mucus' and 'background' in H&E appearance; 'background' is a catch-all for non-tissue or artifact regions; 'cancer-associated stroma' and 'smooth muscle' can be visually indistinguishable at patch level without architectural context; 'normal colon mucosa' vs. 'colorectal adenocarcinoma epithelium' has a dysplastic transition zone that is inherently ambiguous at the 96×96 patch resolution used in PathMNIST. (2) Distribution shift: train and val class proportions are nearly identical (max |Δ| < 0.001), but the test set (CRC-VAL-HE-7K, different clinical center) deviates substantially—adipose prevalence nearly doubles (10.4%→18.6%, ratio 1.79), mucus rises (8.9%→14.4%, ratio 1.62), while debris drops sharply (11.5%→4.7%, ratio 0.41), cancer-associated stroma drops (10.4%→5.9%, ratio 0.56), and smooth muscle drops (13.5%→8.2%, ratio 0.61). This is not a random sampling artifact; it reflects a different tissue-sampling or slide-preparation protocol at the external center. (3) Domain shift: the test set explicitly originates from a different clinical center, introducing uncontrolled variation in H&E staining intensity/hue, scanner color calibration, slide thickness, and fixation quality. The 'debris' class collapse (ratio 0.41) is consistent with different slide-preparation or scanning artifacts at the new site, meaning the model's learned 'debris' features may not transfer. (4) The test set is also smaller (7,180 vs. 89,996 train), amplifying the statistical impact of the skewed distribution and reducing per-class test samples for the under-represented classes (debris n=339, cancer-associated stroma n=421, smooth muscle n=592), making per-class test metrics noisy and less reliable. (5) No information is provided about whether the external center used the same annotation protocol, inter-annotator agreement, or whether 'debris' and 'background' were defined identically, compounding the label-ambiguity risk under domain shift.
ambiguity_risks: Test-set class distribution deviates substantially from train/val (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56), indicating non-random sampling or different tissue-sampling protocol at the external center.
External clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) introduces uncontrolled H&E staining, scanner, and slide-preparation variability that can shift pixel-level features for all classes.

'Debris' is a non-standard, poorly defined histological label that overlaps with 'mucus' and 'background'; its 59% prevalence drop in test suggests the external site's artifact profile differs, undermining label transferability.

'Cancer-associated stroma' vs. 'smooth muscle' and 'normal colon mucosa' vs. 'adenocarcinoma epithelium' are inherently ambiguous at 96×96 patch resolution without multi-scale architectural context, increasing misclassification risk under domain shift.
Small per-class test counts for debris (n=339), stroma (n=421), and smooth muscle (n=592) make per-class test metrics statistically noisy and sensitive to a handful of mislabeled patches.

No evidence that the external center used the same annotation guidelines or inter-annotator agreement process, so label semantics for ambiguous classes (debris, background, stroma) may differ across sites.

The near-identical train/val split (max proportion difference <0.001) suggests a random split of a single-site dataset, meaning the only true external generalization test is the skewed CRC-VAL-HE-7K set, which conflates distribution shift with domain shift.

Patch-level classification without spatial context means the model cannot leverage tissue architecture to disambiguate stroma from smooth muscle or dysplastic from normal epithelium, a limitation that is exacerbated when staining appearance shifts across centers.

dataset_manifest.test_domain_note: CRC-VAL-HE-7K test images originate from a different clinical center.

config.rationale: Second-chance transformer probe. The best compact_transformer (compact_tf_p4, 0.9664) used hidden=96, depth=4, cls pooling, hflip+rotate90. The worse variant (compact_tf_p2_mean, 0.9463) lost ~2% by switching to mean pooling and removing augmentations, confirming cls pooling and spatial aug are essential at 49 tokens. This candidate increases depth 4→6 to give the self-attention more sequential refinement passes over the 49 tokens, while keeping hidden=96 (the width that worked) and num_heads=4 (96/4=24, valid). lr raised 0.0003→0.0005 to maintain effective learning rate across the extra layers. Retains adamw with decoupled wd=0.05 (appropriate for transformer weight decay), cosine schedule, batch 64 (smaller batch stabilizes attention gradients with few tokens), and the proven augmentation set. If this still trails the residual_cnn by >1.5%, it confirms the architecture gap is structural (local inductive bias vs. global attention at 28×28) rather than a hyperparameter issue.

config.rationale: Directly addresses the token-starvation hypothesis: round-1 compact_tf_p4 used patch_size=4 yielding only 49 tokens, which is below the threshold where self-attention learns meaningful relational structure. Switching to patch_size=2 produces 196 tokens (14×14 grid), giving attention 4× more pairwise interactions. Hidden increased to 128 (divisible by 4 heads, multiple of 8) to match the larger token budget and provide adequate per-token representation. Pooling switched from 'cls' to 'mean' to aggregate spatial information across all 196 tokens rather than relying on a single learned CLS token, which is more robust at this resolution. Depth kept at 4 to avoid overfitting with 90k samples. AdamW with wd=0.05 (decoupled weight decay) and cosine schedule retained from the round-1 transformer recipe. Batch size 64 keeps attention gradients stable with the larger token sequence. Dropout kept low (0.1) to preserve the already-limited attention signal.

config.rationale: Best transformer option at 28×28 per research guidance. patch_size=4 yields 49 tokens—enough for meaningful self-attention while keeping parameters modest. hidden=96 (divisible by num_heads=4, multiple of 8) with 4 layers and mlp_ratio=4 gives a compact but expressive attention model. Lower lr (3e-4) and higher weight decay (0.05) with AdamW follow transformer-specific recommendations. Batch 64 stabilises attention gradients with few tokens. Dropout kept at 0.1 to avoid suppressing the limited attention signal. Learned positional encoding suits the small 7×7 grid. Gradient clipping at 1.0 prevents instability with low token counts.

config.rationale: Primary architecture per research priorities. 4 residual blocks with hidden=64 exploit local structure at 28×28 without over-parameterisation. AdamW with cosine decay at lr=1e-3 follows the recommended CNN starting point. Low weight decay (1e-4) avoids over-regularising the subtle channel-variance signal. Class weighting addresses the 1.63× imbalance. Dropout 0.2 on the classifier head provides mild regularisation without suppressing features. Batch 128 balances gradient noise and throughput. Mild augmentations (hflip, rotate90) expand the effective dataset without destroying spatial detail.

config.rationale: Extends the round-1 winner (res_cnn_base, 0.9875) by increasing depth 4→6 and hidden 64→96 to capture richer hierarchical local features at 28×28. The extra two residual blocks add capacity without over-parameterisation (96 channels × 6 blocks is still modest for 90k samples). LR reduced to 8e-4 for training stability at greater depth. Dropout raised to 0.25 to regularise the larger model. Brightness augmentation added (3rd augmentation) to counteract the very low channel stds (0.12–0.18) and expose the model to intensity variation. Weight decay nudged to 2e-4 for mild L2 regularisation. Cosine schedule and AdamW retained as the proven pair from round 1. Early stopping patience of 5 epochs gives the deeper network more room to converge before stopping.

config.rationale: Explores a fundamentally different optimization trajectory for the same residual_cnn architecture that won round 1. SGD with momentum and a one-cycle LR schedule (peak 0.01) tends to find flatter minima than Adam, which can improve generalization on the 10k validation set. The larger batch size (256) stabilizes SGD's noisier gradients. Label smoothing reduced to 0.05 since SGD's implicit regularization (from its larger effective step size and momentum) provides additional smoothing. Dropout lowered to 0.15 to avoid over-regularising in combination with SGD's natural regularisation. Weight decay at 5e-4 is modest and appropriate for SGD. Three augmentations (hflip, vflip, rotate90) provide geometric diversity. This candidate tests whether the round-1 AdamW optimum is a local optimum that SGD can escape, while keeping the architecture identical to isolate the optimizer/scheduler effect.

config.rationale: Fast, low-risk baseline to establish a performance floor and validate hyperparameter choices. hidden=32 with 3 layers keeps the model small and fast to train, enabling quick iteration. Slightly higher lr (2e-3) compensates for the smaller capacity. Larger batch (256) reduces gradient noise for the simpler architecture. Dropout 0.3 provides stronger regularisation appropriate for the smaller model. Three augmentations (hflip, vflip, rotate90) maximise data diversity for the limited capacity. This candidate serves as a reference point: if residual_cnn or compact_transformer do not substantially outperform it, the added complexity is not justified.
